title: Reduce flakiness of tests
description:
I observed 1-2% flakiness in the test suite.

 - The default `nbagg = 25L` produces a never-out-of-bag observation about .05% of the time, n=30 should be about an order magnitude rarer and not slow down the test much
 - [{ipred}'s `predict.classbagg` method uses `sample()` in the case of ties](https://codeberg.org/thothorn/ipred/src/commit/d0199232dd65e13cdd6e6e07f80505445b712971/R/predict.bagging.R#L7), leading to a 1-2% rate of the predictions differing purely by chance. (I suppose an alternative is to use a different `aggregation=`)

All told I see 1/10000 failure with this change (the 1 would go away at `nbagg=35L`)

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to butcher website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the butcher website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: add butcher methods for mixOmics output
description:
These methods do a good job of being selective about what they bring along from the enclosing env, and do make use of most all of the heavier bits of inputted data that they retain at predict time—not a lot of memory released, in the end.

`mixo_plsda` objects are a subclass of `mixo_pls`, so don’t need their own methods!

The mixOmics package is hosted on Bioconductor rather than CRAN, so this PR doesn’t introduce mixOmics as a dependency. This also means that mixOmics methods won’t be tested on CRAN or CI.

``` r
library(butcher)
library(mixOmics)
#> Loading required package: MASS
#> Loading required package: lattice
#> Loading required package: ggplot2
#> 
#> Loaded mixOmics 6.20.0
#> Thank you for using mixOmics!
#> Tutorials: http://mixomics.org
#> Bookdown vignette: https://mixomicsteam.github.io/Bookdown
#> Questions, issues: Follow the prompts at http://mixomics.org/contact-us
#> Cite us:  citation('mixOmics')

fit_mod <- function() {
  boop <- runif(1e6)
  pls(matrix(rnorm(2e4), ncol = 2), rnorm(1e4), mode = "classic")
}

mod_fit <- fit_mod()
mod_res <- butcher(mod_fit)

weigh(mod_fit)
#> # A tibble: 24 × 2
#>    object             size
#>    <chr>             <dbl>
#>  1 X              0.801   
#>  2 variates.X     0.801   
#>  3 variates.Y     0.801   
#>  4 Y              0.721   
#>  5 names.sample   0.640   
#>  6 input.X        0.161   
#>  7 call           0.00129 
#>  8 loadings.X     0.000776
#>  9 loadings.Y     0.000696
#> 10 loadings.star1 0.0006  
#> # … with 14 more rows
weigh(mod_res)
#> # A tibble: 24 × 2
#>    object              size
#>    <chr>              <dbl>
#>  1 X               0.801   
#>  2 variates.X      0.801   
#>  3 variates.Y      0.801   
#>  4 Y               0.721   
#>  5 loadings.X      0.000776
#>  6 loadings.Y      0.000696
#>  7 loadings.star1  0.0006  
#>  8 mat.c           0.0006  
#>  9 loadings.star2  0.00052 
#> 10 prop_expl_var.X 0.000352
#> # … with 14 more rows

new_data <- matrix(1:2, ncol = 2)
colnames(new_data) <- c("X1", "X2")

testthat::expect_equal(
  purrr::discard_at(predict(mod_fit, new_data), "call"),
  purrr::discard_at(predict(mod_res, new_data), "call")
)
```

title: add butcher methods for `ipred::bagging()`
description:
Related to #234. Same story with NEWS!

`ipred::bagging` can return `regbagg`, `classbagg`, or `survbagg` objects. This PR relocates the classbagg butcher methods to a more general `ipred` file that includes support for the other types of objects returned by the same method.

These objects store a bunch of `rpart` output in a nested list, so these methods just iterate through and dispatch to `axe_*.rpart()`.

``` r
library(butcher)
library(ipred)

fit_mod <- function() {
  boop <- runif(1e6)
  bagging(y ~ x, data.frame(y = rnorm(1e4), x = rnorm(1e4)))
}

mod_fit <- fit_mod()
mod_res <- butcher(mod_fit)

weigh(mod_fit)
```

title: Set up for "hard" R CMD check
Add support for k-Prototypes clustering
description:
This PR aims to extend `butcher` so it can also handle k-Prototypes clustering (`kproto`) models from the [`clustMixType`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/clustMixType/) package.

The largest elements within a kproto object are:

- cluster - holds predicted clusters for every training data point
- dists - matrix of size number of training samples `x` number of clusters
- data - training data

When those objects are axed the size of the `kproto` model object is reduced considerably and `predict()` runs just fine.

However, running `validation_kproto()`, `summary()` and `clprofiles()` on the reduced object is infeasible.

Also resolves #31  

Focus here is on the `train` and `train.recipes` object. The former sub-axe methods classified as `misc` are removed. The key sub-axe function for these model objects lies in `axe_env`, so attention was paid to ensure all possible environments were replaced with either `rlang::empty_env()` or `rlang::base_env()` without breaking downstream functions like `predict`.

title: Remove env srcref
description:
The environment referenced as a result of source references can be removed as explored below: 

```{r}
# Load something to test
y <- butcher::butcher_example("train.rda")
load(y)
x <- train_fit

# See envs for one component of modelInfo
str(x$modelInfo$grid)

# Size
lobstr::obj_size(x$modelInfo$grid)
# 51,744 B

# Check out what's in the env 
mode(attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile)
ls(attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile)

# Each element listed
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$Enc
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$filename
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$fixedNewlines
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$isFile
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$lines
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$parseData
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$timestamp
attributes(attributes(x$modelInfo$grid)$srcref)$srcfile$wd

# Strip it out
attributes(x$modelInfo$grid) <- NULL
lobstr::obj_size(x$modelInfo$grid)
# 51,440 B
```

While the memory saved appears minor, when envs are removed from all the components of `modelInfo` we get: 

```{r}
lobstr::obj_size(x$modelInfo)
# 85,512 B
temp <- purrr::map(x$modelInfo, function(z) axe_env(z))
lobstr::obj_size(temp)
# 83,688 B
```
